newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobless rate seen easing later next year.
newsitem.headline: German jobless rate seen easing later next year.

text.p: Germany's jobless rate, perched at a post-unification record, may be on the verge of improving next year even though it may first get worse, politicians said at the weekend.

"I see an impending change in the situation on the German labour market," Wolfgang Schaeuble, the powerful parliamentary leader for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, told German paper Bild am Sonntag. A summary of the article was released ahead of time.
But rough winter weather could force the jobless rate, at 4.1 million in November, to climb more, he added.
CDU politician Friedhelm Ost told the Neue Osnabruecker Zeitung a cold winter could raise the unemployment rate to 4.5 million by the end of February.
The head of Germany's labour office, Bernhard Jagoda, made the same prediction a week ago.

Schaeuble, however, stuck by his party's goal to halve Germany's jobless rate by the year 2000 and urged companies to create more jobs. He welcome signs that German companies were starting to rethink strategies that their immediate obligation would be to boost profits and please shareholders.
Ost predicted a change in trend next autumn and criticised companies for setting incorrect priorities.

Urging groups "to make the impossible possible," he said it was unacceptable for German managers to spend more time sorting out their recreation schedules than on creating marketing strategies for new products.

In an opinion piece to be published in Sunday's edition of the Frankfurter Allgemein Sonntagszeitung, Reinhard Goehner, a senior official at Germany's federal employer association, urged a restructuring of unemployment insurance as well as re-training schemes and job-creationg schemes.
A summary of the article was made available ahead of time.
